The 10-session horizon now matures on 10 December and for the first time in this ledger it contains three first-tier events rather than one: the November employment report on 4 December, the FOMC decision with projections on 9 December, and November CPI at 8:30am on 10 December - the maturity morning itself. Gold's stretch reading improves two notches to -3 (extreme-down) from the -5 that was the deepest in this ledger's record, and both components that switched off did so narrowly: RSI went from 29.62 to 31.93, back above 30, and the range component turned off by 15 basis points - the close sits 2.015% above the 252-session closing low of 3515.40 against a 2.0% trigger, where a close of 3585.71 or below - 49 cents lower - would have kept it firing. The overlay changes five of eighteen cells, the most in this ledger's record, and it contains three outright vetoes. Gold's 1-session bearish call arrives at exactly margin 4 while riding an extreme-down reading - the stretch-v1 veto condition - and is vetoed to flat-lean; its 5- and 10-session bearish calls ride the same reading at margins 7 and 8 and are each dampened one notch, from strong to solid. The Nasdaq-100's 1-session and 10-session cells both resolve bearish at exactly margin 4 while riding an extreme-down reading of -3, so both are vetoed to flat-lean as well; its 5-session cell was already flat on the tally. Nothing else qualifies: the S&P 500's and Russell 2000's cells all resolve flat or no-call, which the overlay leaves alone by construction, and the dollar's extreme-up +3 touches nothing because two of its three cells fall below the live gate and the third is flat. So the headline for the day is that the vote model wanted three bearish calls it did not get: gold at one session and the Nasdaq-100 at one and ten sessions were all bearish before the overlay and are flat after it.

Six of eighteen cells resolve to no-call on the live gate: all three bonds cells, the dollar's 1- and 10-session cells, and the Russell 2000's 10-session cell. For bonds this is mechanical rather than a change in evidence: category 13's hourly and weekly reads both compute choppy this session, so the weight-3 mechanical vote contributes nothing to the live count, and with Breadth, Sentiment, Earnings and Seasonality all structurally neutral for a Treasury note, seven of the fifteen available weight is unreachable before any judgment is applied - the asset cannot clear a gate of 7 unless almost every remaining category votes directionally. For the dollar the cause is the vendor disagreement over the index's own daily sign described in its nullInputs: with four sources spanning 0.28 points and two of them disagreeing on direction, Breadth, Volatility regime, Sentiment, Positioning and Cross-asset all vote neutral rather than lean on an unresolved input, which leaves the 1-session cell at live 3 and the 10-session cell at live 6, one short. Its 5-session cell clears at exactly 7 and resolves flat at margin 3, with Trend structure and Fed path bullish against Rates and Cross-asset bearish.

newsLog.event: October PCE, the last major inflation print before the Dec 8-9 FOMC, came in hot. Headline PCE rose to 3.8% y/y, the highest annual reading since 2023, and core PCE accelerated to 3.3% y/y, above the 3.2% consensus and up from 3.1% in September. Consumer spending rose 0.3% m/m after an upwardly revised 0.6% in September. Traders now price a ~98% chance of a 25bp December rate HIKE from the current 3.75%-4.00% range, with another increase expected in January; Governor Waller has signaled he could back 50bp.
newsLog.numbers: Headline PCE +0.3% m/m (est +0.3%), +3.8% y/y vs 3.6% prior. Core PCE +0.3% m/m (est +0.3%), +3.3% y/y vs est 3.2% and 3.1% prior. Consumer spending +0.3% m/m (Sept revised to +0.6% from +0.5%). CME FedWatch: ~98% odds of a 25bp Dec 8-9 hike. Pre-release: 10Y 4.85% (lowest since Nov 9), 2Y 4.600%; post-print quote 10Y 4.844% (-6bp)
newsLog.reaction: The wrong kind of hot: an upside core print with a December hike already fully priced, so the pressure landed on equities rather than the front end. Yields actually fell in a bull steepening as growth fears drove haven demand (10Y -6bp to 4.844%), while gold slid 2.35% to 3,506.70 near a 14-month low and the VIX jumped 18.6% to 31.27. Equity futures extended losses after the release.

newsLog.event: The Trump administration proposed new tariffs of up to 20% on China, the EU and 12 other major trading partners, following an eight-month USTR investigation into excess manufacturing capacity and industrial subsidies. The duties would stack on existing tariffs, pushing total rates above 40% in some categories, with China expected to face the higher end. Final rates are not set: the proposal goes through hearings and a public comment period and an official said it would likely take effect in January at the earliest. The existing US-China trade truce expires January 10.
newsLog.numbers: Proposed rate: up to 20%, stacking to above 40% total in some areas; 14 economies covered (China, EU + 12 others); 8-month USTR probe; earliest effective date January 2027; China truce expiry Jan 10. Futures at 07:13 ET: Nasdaq 100 -782 pts (-3%), S&P 500 -144 pts (-2%), Dow -646 pts (-1.3%), Russell 2000 -1.39%
newsLog.reaction: Tariff headlines hit a tape already unwinding the AI trade, and the combination with hot PCE produced a broad risk-off open: Nasdaq 100 futures -3%, S&P 500 -2%, Dow -1.3%, Russell 2000 -1.4%, VIX above 31. Semis took the brunt on fears the measures eventually reach chip supply chains; the January timeline and comment period leave room for the scope to be negotiated down.

newsLog.event: Monday's Jensen Huang-return melt-up has fully reversed into a global chip rout. Asia closed sharply lower: the Kospi plunged 6.16% to its weakest close since Jan 13, triggering a sell-side sidecar on the Korea Exchange, while SoftBank sank about 14.8% to a 52-week low and dragged the Nikkei down 2.8%. Nvidia, which fell 5.9% on Tuesday, dropped another 5-6% premarket, with AMD, Intel, Micron and Dell all down more. Investors are again questioning the payoff on AI infrastructure spending and circular financing, with Anthropic trading below its $83 IPO price.

newsLog.event: The BEA's second estimate put Q3 real GDP growth at a 4.3% annualized rate, a large upward revision from the 3.4% advance estimate and above the ~3.5% consensus, versus 2.2% in Q2. Quarterly core PCE was 2.5%, in line, and the GDP price index came in at 1.8%, below the 2.3% consensus. The release landed alongside October PCE at 8:30 AM ET, reinforcing the picture John Williams described on Tuesday: a strong economy with inflation still running too hot.
newsLog.numbers: Q3 real GDP +4.3% annualized (second estimate) vs +3.4% advance and ~3.5% consensus; Q2 +2.2%. Q3 core PCE +2.5% (est 2.5%); Q3 GDP price index +1.8% (est 2.3%)
newsLog.reaction: Growth this strong removes the last excuse for the Fed not to hike in December and is the main reason a 25bp move is ~98% priced. Equities read it as a tightening signal rather than an earnings tailwind; the softer deflator is the only dovish detail and was swamped by the hot monthly core PCE released the same minute.
newsLog.vsExp: GDP 4.3% vs ~3.5% expected (big upside beat); Q3 core PCE in line at 2.5%; deflator 1.8% vs 2.3% expected (cooler)
